An insert costs one round, like a move.

optional_picks.says: Run this step only when an earlier step came out a certain way. {"step": 3, "outcome": "no_reply"}. The outcome is one of: replied, no_reply, done, not_done, yes, no. Add "after_days" (1 to 30) to wait that long before it is decided, e.g. {"step": 3, "outcome": "no_reply", "after_days": 3}. On a step that repeats for each item of that same step, it is checked for each item.

Only when who is "person". What the person does, with a link they tap and what it costs them before they tap: {"link": "https://...", "cost_cents": 10000, "cost_note": "about $100 a month"}. The link is the page where the person does it, in the service itself, not a help article.

A tool from this want's list, or any service by name. A name that is not on the list is declared as an outside act for you: you say what you will do, the person taps Allow, and your evidence comes back through the evidence door. IT ALSO TAKES A LIST, in the order the calls should run, all on ONE account: ["composio:<service>/<TOOL_A>", "composio:<service>/<TOOL_B>"]. One account row, one card, one approval, and a later call can read what an earlier one came back with. To bind one, write the entry with its own arguments: {"tool": "composio:<service>/<TOOL_B>", "args": {"id": {"$from": "<tool_a>.id"}}} where <tool_a> is the earlier tool's name in lower case with underscores. Supply required arguments as actual values or valid bindings; missing inputs return their field schema. A typed binding is a JSON object {"$from":"source.field"}, not "$ref" or a quoted JSON object. It preserves the source value's type; {{source.field}} interpolates text and cannot carry an object. Sources are person.<question id> for an actual answer, draft.words for the words you supplied, or <earlier run name>.<field> for an actual result on this same step. The document shows the generated run names. Never invent a source or use steps.N.output. For values produced by an earlier STEP, have that step file structured cards items containing the needed fields, then set the consuming form step's repeats to {"cadence":"for_each","of_step":N}, where N is that earlier step's one-based document number. Bind its fields with {"$from":"item.<field>"}. This also works for one item. The platform supplies handover.N as the list; do not bind handover.N.<field>. The producer must actually supply the required value in the tool's expected shape before execution. Do not invent a date or other value just to pass validation.
Only on a "posts" step whose room needs a name (a Slack channel, a Discord channel id, a subreddit): which one. The form asks it as a blank there; LinkedIn and X never need it.

How often this step runs: {"cadence": "for_each", "of_step": 4} to do it once for every item step 4 handed over, or {"cadence": "for_each", "of_step": "who"} to do it once for each person picked on the who step. By default you write every item as soon as the step opens and the person approves them one at a time; add "pace": "all_at_once" for one approval of the whole list, or "pace": "after_each" if the next item depends on how the last one came out. Each item's result (replied, no_reply, done, not_done, yes, no) can be read by a later step's only_if. "daily", "weekly" and "each_time" are recorded on the step but not run yet: the step runs once. For a daily drip of content, hand over the whole package and the platform delivers it on its schedule.

ONLY on a `posts` step, and there it is asked as a blank: the words that go in the post. The person reads those exact words and taps once; we add the line saying an AI wrote it and who for. Nobody but you can write them, so they are the one piece of a post the bench cannot stamp for you.

What you need FROM THE PERSON before this step can run, one entry per thing: [{"name": "shop_link", "label": "The exact link to your shop", "kind": "link"}]. `kind` is one of: text, number, yes_no, choice, file, link (text is the default); a `choice` carries two or more "options", a `number` may carry a "unit". A plain string is an ask too and means a text one. Up to 8 per step, labels up to 140 characters. THE BENCH BUILDS THE STEP: the person gets a step of their own, right before yours, with one box per entry, and their answers come back to you by name -- bind one in an act's arguments as {"$from": "person.<name>"}, the same way person.who works. Never ask the person for information on a step of YOURS: your step is where they approve what you did with their answers.
The number of the step in your own proposal this came from, if it came from one. Everything you already wrote on that step is carried across.
